config.prompt: Explain, in a few paragraphs, how a write-ahead log lets a database recover after a crash.

reference.text:
When a user inserts, updates, or deletes a row in a database, the write-ahead log is used to record those operations. Essentially, the write-ahead log is a sequential file that is written to after every operation. This ensures that any changes made to the database are recorded before the data is written to the database’s main storage.
The write-ahead log file is a buffer cache that permits all changes made to the database, but are not yet stored in the main data storage. When a database is started, it reads the write-ahead log file and applies any outstanding operations to the database. This ensures that changes made before the crash will be replayed so that the database is returned to the state it was in at the time of the crash.
When a database crashes, the write-ahead log is used as a recovery mechanism to ensure that the database is consistent. The database reads the write-ahead log file, applies the operations, and thus recovers the data that was lost in the crash. This ensures that any insert, update, or delete operation made before the crash will be reflected in the database after recovery. It also prevents any partial or inconsistent operations from being reflected in the database, which would make it unpredictable and unreliable.

**Write-Ahead Log**

A write-ahead log is a file that stores all changes made to a database's data files before they are actually written to the data files. When a database transaction is committed, it also writes the transaction's changes to the write-ahead log. This ensures that a change is written to the log before it is written to the data files.

The write-ahead log is stored on disk, and is protected from crashes. After a crash, the database can use the write-ahead log to restore its state to a consistent point in time. When the database restarts, it can recover its data by replaying the contents of the write-ahead log. This is where the interaction with the data files occurs.
